inputs.prompt: Produce a French version, in Québec usage and the register of a {{inputs.documentKind}}, of the document below. Keep the structure, numbers, dates, amounts and defined terms exactly. Use the firm glossary when given: {{inputs.glossary}}. Document: {{inputs.document}}. The first line of your answer is exactly this sentence: fr « Traduction automatisée non certifiée — à faire réviser par un professionnel avant tout usage, surtout pour un document juridique. » en « Automated, uncertified translation — to be reviewed by a professional before any use, above all for a legal document. » (use the one that matches the output language). Mark anything you are unsure of as « À réviser » (fr) or « To review » (en). Name the terminology source of every term you choose (the usage recommended by the Office québécois de la langue française, OQLF, and its Grand dictionnaire terminologique, when one applies; otherwise say « usage courant »). Never invent a legal term: when no established Québec term exists, keep the source term in brackets and flag the passage. Never quote a statute; refer to it by name only.

From the source document {{inputs.document}} and this French version {{steps.translation.content}}, list the terms you chose as a table: Source term | French term | Source of the term | Doubt (yes/no). Then list the doubtful passages, each with a one-line reason.
